applicabilityBasis.summary: USX is marketed as a dollar-tracking medium of exchange and the settlement/payment rail of the Solstice protocol. The current protocol whitepaper names USX Ltd as the ring-fenced vehicle that mints and redeems USX, while the platform terms describe issuance and 1:1 redemption through Solstice Foundation accounts. Institutional redemption documentation specifies USDG rather than national currency. Apparent-payment-stablecoin is retained as a product screening classification, not a finding that every element of GENIUS section 2(22) is legally satisfied: redemption solely in another digital asset does not itself establish the required fixed monetary-value obligation.

genius.notes: Re-verified 2026-10-07. issuerEntity changes from Solstice Foundation to USX Ltd because the current protocol whitepaper expressly identifies USX Ltd as the USX mint/redeem issuance vehicle; Foundation remains the governance body and platform contracting party. Domicile is unset: the BVI jurisdiction of Equinox Strategies Ltd or SLX Ltd cannot be transferred to USX Ltd. Although the current document URL contains Whitepaper 2.1, the fetched document identifies itself as May 2026/v2.0; the researcher's unsupported 2026-09-01 sourceDate is removed. The institutions page claims EU/EEA passporting and MiCA compliance, while terms restrict EEA/UK-directed services. ESMA OTHER.csv and the cited MiCA whitepaper concern SLX issued by SLX Ltd, not USX, and Title II notification is not token issuer authorization. No U.S. GENIUS authorization or registered foreign exception was located. The Accountable API returned reserve/liability data, supporting disclosure-hub presence; continuous proof-of-solvency data is not an independent monthly reserve attestation. No such monthly report was located.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of 2026-10-07, no public GENIUS permitted-issuer approval, state qualification, official GENIUS application or OCC foreign-issuer registration naming USX Ltd or Solstice Foundation for USX was located in the sources checked. The OCC table covers pending digital-asset licensing applications, not an exhaustive GENIUS issuer register. Indexed searches and issuer silence do not establish that no unindexed or nonpublic filing exists. Foreign-exception status remains unknown; no inference of non-compliance is made.
